what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 2 of 2: A ledger whose requirement reads the bond energy: can it demand the walk's lattice force exactly?. SETTING (the moving-records column and the amplitude layer under the owner's reading; open PRs #8931 (block 104: the rule's own clock has no far field; the pull needs a rate law with a monopole, a rest energy and gamma), block 105 (in discrete ticks a local clock is exact only for walks that do not move; the partial-swap walk follows block 54's clock to relative eps^2), block 106 (no local momentum falls with weight one on the lattice - the weight is the slope of its band value, with zero zone mean; the force is a bond energy times a clock difference), #8570 (block 54: the clocked walk), #8571 (block 55: the ledger and gamma), #8597 (block 66: the fall and the ledger), #8612 (block 77: the staggered rest term), #8611 (block 76: an induced gamma), #8860 (block 95: records on their own clocks) - find the unnumbered ones with gh pr list --search 'admissibility induced-law block 105' etc.; ALL clauses supplied, nothing adopted; read the notes on their PR branches before starting). TASK: block 106 T2-T3: the walk's force is exactly f_j(x) = d_j phi(x) eps_j(x) + d_j phi(x - e_j) eps_j(x - e_j), eps_b the bond cross energy; ledgers built from curls demand no force, and rate-carrying ledgers with requirements in (energy density, current) cannot match it at every wave number. (a) Construct a relabelling ledger with a field that couples to eps_b (a bond field), keeping block 64's relabelling blindness and the rates' covariance, whose static equations demand exactly the walk's f at every state; or (b) prove no ledger with local fields does. HIT: (a) or (b) exact. DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/a-ledger-that-reads-bond-energies/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --model <model> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/derive/a-ledger-that-reads-bond-energies/<name>/check.py"
